gary_2026_10_04_cast_gny_startup_pitch_c.summary: Gary's Guide: Innovate. Pitch. Impact. Join the CASTGNY Startup Pitch Competition on October 4, 2026, in the heart of Manhattan! This event brings together aspiring founders, entrepreneurs, investors, & industry professionals for a morning of pitching, feedback, networking, & practical insights into building & growing a startup. This is an opportunity to showcase your idea, learn from experienced professionals, & connect with the Greater New York innovation community. Grand Prizes A Mac Mini M6 for the winning team! Tentative Agenda 9:30 - 9:45 AM Check-in & Networking 9:45 - 9:50 AM Welcome Remarks 9:50 - 10:10 AM Lightning Pitch Workshop 10:10 - 10:20 AM Introduction to the Startup Pitch Competition - Rules, format & judging criteria 10:20 - 11:30 AM Startup Pitch Competition - Startup pitches & judges' Q&A 11:30 - 11:40 AM Judges' Deliberation 11:40 AM - 12:25 PM Entrepreneurship & Innovation Discussion- Insights from founders, investors, scientists & technology leaders 12:25 - 12:30 PM Award Ceremony & Grand Prize Presentation (Agenda is subject to change.) Want to Pitch? Register on Luma to attend the event. You will receive a link to submit your full application. You will be asked to submit: Project Name Elevator Pitch About the Project (what inspired you, what you learned, how you built your project, & the challenges you faced) Built with (what tools, what models, what languages, ...) "Try it out" Links (links to your prototype, business, ...) Image Gallery (up to 15 images) Video Demo Link Current Stage: Prototype / MVP Early users / Pilot Revenue-generating Other Industry / Category: AI / Software Healthcare / Biotech FinTech Education Consumer Sustainability / Climate Hardware Other Supplementary Materials

gary_2026_10_04_brderless_buildathon_ai_.title: Brderless Buildathon - AI Agents
gary_2026_10_04_brderless_buildathon_ai_.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_10_04_brderless_buildathon_ai_.summary: Gary's Guide: Brderless Buildathon: AI Agents - NYC Most hackathons end at the demo. We built this differently. The Brderless Buildathon is a two-part format: a curated 24-hour build in New York, then two weeks to keep shipping, then a Demo Day where the selected winning teams show a real product. Part 1 - The Buildathon (October 4) 100 vetted builders. One theme: AI agents that do real work - planning, tool use, multi-step execution, human-in-the-loop. Not chatbots. The day: 10:00am: Doors open, breakfast 11:00am: Keynote from speakers & team formation 12:00pm: Lunch & build 3:00pm: Project check-ins 4:00pm: Submissions close & final selections 5:00pm: Judging round one, awards, & selection of the teams advancing to Part 2 Food & caffeine for the full 24. Top teams advance to part 2. Part 2 - Demo Day (October 8) Selected teams get two weeks & mentor support + credits to turn the weekend into a product. Then they demo live to a curated room of investors, operators, & sponsors - 7-min demo, 5-min Q&A. Who should apply? Engineers, technical founders, AI/agents engineers, & product people who ship. Solo, with a team, or matched with one - all fine. If you come as a pair or group, please make sure that everyone registers. About the Hosts & Sponsors Brderless brings together the most extraordinary founders & builders through a carefully curated community.

gary_2026_10_06_tech_x_market_decoders_l.title: Tech x Market Decoders - Let's Talk About Jev
gary_2026_10_06_tech_x_market_decoders_l.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_10_06_tech_x_market_decoders_l.summary: Gary's Guide: We decode tech & market signals together, salon-style with a curated group - so you can operate, invest, & decide better. Past attendees have been founders, investors & operators who work in tech or tech-adjacent roles across industries - Our Why AI can build a financial model, summarize an earnings call, or map a competitive landscape in seconds. What AI cannot do is connect the dots around what's happening right now - a technology, a trend, a business, an idea, a decision. Or what a moment like that actually signals. That takes human judgment, experience, & taste. The kind you only build by studying real examples, arguing them out loud, & testing your read against people who see it differently than you do. If you want a space to actually grow your thinking IRL & connect with people who match that energy, this is it. That's what Tech x Market Decoders is for. Every week, we pick one topic - a company or startup everyone's talking about, a technology reshaping an industry, or a shift in how things are being built or bought. Bring your laptop. Here's how it works: Check-in & Intros 15 minutes - decode solo. Quick research time. Dig into the news, the product, the tech, the data. 45 minutes - decode together. We open the floor. What did you find? Where do you disagree? What's convincing, what's overhyped, what would change your mind? This is where judgment actually gets built - not from reading alone, but from testing your read against someone else's. Last few minutes - wrap up. You'll leave with a sharper read on the topic than you walked in with, & a few new perspectives you hadn't considered. That's the whole point. This week's topic: Let's Talk About Jev! A tiny AI startup called Jev just went viral for doing the opposite of what every other AI company is doing - it doesn't chat at all. Built by an ex-OpenAI researcher, Jev only returns fast, structured decisions (yes/no, multiple choice, confidence scores) instead of generating text, & it's reportedly fielding funding offers north of $10 billion just over a week after launch. We're decoding: Is Jev a genuinely new category of AI - a faster, cheaper layer sitting underneath the chatbots - or is this hype-cycle enthusiasm for something that's really just a narrow classifier with good marketing? Supporting questions: Does the "specialized model" approach threaten the big general-purpose LLMs, or complement them? What would it take for Jev's $10B valuation talk to actually make sense a year from now? Come as you are - operator, investor, builder, or just someone who reads too much tech or business news & wants to discuss with smart people. Prep not required but feel free to do some home research before you arrive if you'd like. **Refunds available up to 48 hours before the session. After that, we are sorry but the fee is non-refundable.

gary_2026_10_07_pmai_creativity_business.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_10_07_pmai_creativity_business.summary: Gary's Guide: Creativity & Business Problems in the Age of AI - a workshop for entrepreneurs We are entering a strange moment for creativity. For decades, we have been taught that innovation comes from thinking outside the box, brainstorming more ideas, & waiting for that breakthrough moment. But in the age of AI, & ideas are suddenly abundant, the real challenge is no longer simply coming up with more ideas. It is knowing how to find the right pieces, make unexpected connections, & turn them into something genuinely new & useful. This hands-on workshop, led by our head of program Jeffrey, introduces a practical methodology for doing exactly that. What we'll cover We'll start by looking at some of the traditional assumptions behind creativity & innovation: brainstorming, originality, intuition, & the idea of the lone creative genius, & why some of those assumptions are becoming less useful in an AI-native world. We'll then introduce a different way to approach creative problem-solving: instead of trying to invent the answer from scratch, you'll learn how to break a problem apart, deliberately search for useful precedents & ideas, & recombine existing elements in new ways. Through real-world case studies, we'll examine how successful products, businesses, & innovations often emerge not from a completely original idea, but from making the right connection between things that already exist. Most importantly, this will not be a lecture. You'll work through the methodology yourself, apply it to actual business problems, & leave with a framework you can reuse when thinking about products, positioning, growth, operations, or your next startup idea. Who should attend This workshop is designed primarily for: Early-stage founders, aspiring entrepreneurs, small business owners, product builders, & operators who regularly need to solve ambiguous problems with limited resources. No technical background is required. If you have ever stared at a blank page thinking, I need a better idea, this workshop is for you. Come with a problem. Leave with a different way of thinking about it.

gary_2026_10_08_against_the_inevitable_f.summary: Gary's Guide: We can do something about it, actually!Frontier AI companies are relying on the inevitability narrative to push every sector to adopt their techuse their products, or get left behind. gary_2026_10_08_the_ai_founder_playbook_.title: The AI Founder Playbook, Rewritten
gary_2026_10_08_the_ai_founder_playbook_.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_10_08_the_ai_founder_playbook_.summary: Gary's Guide: Invitation only 15 seats Approval required For leaders of Series A+ startups building proprietary AI models, with a select number of seats reserved for investors. This is a roundtable, not a panel: everyone at the table is welcome to bring opinions. Some of the investors in the room: Merck Global Health Innovation Fund (GHI Fund) Presidio Ventures (Sumitomo Corporation) Morgan Stanley Ventures Lab Description: When AI compresses engineering cycles from months to days, the scarcest thing in a startup is no longer the ability to build. It's knowing what to build, for whom, & how to win when everyone can ship. That shift rewrites the founder's job. Moats move from code to data, distribution, & judgment. Team shapes change. Capital efficiency changes what "venture scale" even means. The playbooks most of us learned are quietly going out of date, & the new ones are being written right now, by the people in rooms like this one. The evening: Dinner & conversation with a curated table of ~15 founders, operators, & investors. Exceptional wines, thoughtfully curated cuisine, & original artwork. Guests will experience a thoughtfully curated progression of refined dishes, premium selections, & seasonal ingredients, accompanied by Cava Brut & Ros, Petit Chablis, & Malbec. The evening concludes with an exclusive dessert pairing & the Signature Cocktail, a bespoke finale to the experience. What we'll get into: What's newly easy, what's suddenly hard, & what that does to the first 18 months of a company Where defensibility actually lives when software is cheap How team composition & hiring change when one builder does the work of five What the next generation of founder playbooks will look like House rules: Off the record. No slides, no pitches, no recording. Come with a point of view.

gary_2026_10_10_latinos_x_ai_hackathon.summary: Gary's Guide: Latinos x AI Hackathon - NYC Saturday, October 10 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM New York City Nuestra gente. Nuestros problemas. Nuestro cdigo. For Hispanic Heritage Month, 150 builders are spending one Saturday in New York building AI for the problems our communities actually live with. Not a demo day. Not a panel. Eight hours, three tracks, working software by 5pm. Applications are reviewed. Attendance is free. The Three Tracks Pick one when you apply. Build for it all day. 01 Immigration - Papers & Process Status, documents, deadlines, & the systems that decide who belongs. Think intake triage for legal aid clinics, plain-language explainers for immigration forms, interpreter tooling, case-status tracking, know-your-rights assistants. 02 Healthcare - Care Without Barriers Language, coverage, & access for patients the system was not built for. Think interpretation at the point of care, insurance navigation, discharge instructions people can actually read, community health worker tooling, prescription & benefits literacy. 03 Finance - Banking the Unbanked Credit, remittances, & building wealth without a financial history. Think remittance transparency, credit-building for thin-file borrowers, small business bookkeeping for cash operations, benefits & tax navigation, fraud protection for first-generation account holders. Prizes $4,500 total - $1,500 per track. Every track winner also gets [sponsor perks once confirmed]. Schedule Schedule 10:00 AM - Doors, breakfast, team formation 10:45 AM - Opening remarks & track briefings 11:15 AM - Building starts 1:00 PM - Lunch 3:00 PM - Mentor office hours & mid-day checkpoint 4:45 PM - Submissions close 5:00 PM - Demos on stage 5:45 PM - Judging & awards 6:00 PM - Close Who Should Apply Engineers, data scientists, & designers who want to ship something real in a day Product people & founders who can shape a problem & pitch it Clinicians, immigration attorneys, paralegals, social workers, & financial counselors - the people who know the problem from the inside. You do not need to code to be valuable here. Teams with a domain expert consistently win. Students & career switchers You can apply solo or with a team of up to four. Solo applicants will be matched at 10:00 AM. What to Bring Laptop & charger A problem you have seen up close ID for building security We provide breakfast, lunch, coffee, wifi, power, mentors, & the room. Rules Build during the event. Prior research & planning are fine; prior code is not. Teams of one to four. Every submission needs a public repo, a two-minute demo video, & a short written description. You keep everything you build. No IP claims from organizers or sponsors. Be decent to each other. Harassment of any kind means you leave. No. The event is built by & for the Latino community in New York, & everyone who wants to build for these problems is welcome. Do I need a team? No. Come solo & we will match you at the start. gary_2026_10_11_ai_engineer_kids_day.label: Tech / AI
gary_2026_10_11_ai_engineer_kids_day.summary: Gary's Guide: Welcome to our very first AI Engineer Kids Day in New York City. We're thrilled to have you here! This special event brings together curious young minds & their families for a fun, hands-on introduction to artificial intelligence, coding, & technology. We're especially excited to welcome Cassandra Chin, an outstanding computer science graduate & author, who has led engaging workshops at conferences around the world. Cassandra will guide participants through interactive sessions designed to spark creativity, build confidence, & make complex ideas accessible & fun. These workshops are recommended for kids aged 9 to 15, & parents are encouraged to join. Whether you're completely new to AI or already curious about how things work behind the scenes, this is a chance to learn, explore, & create - together! Agenda 12:30 PM - Doors open & registration - Arrive, check in, & get settled. 1:00 PM - AI Workshop 3:00 PM - Workshop concludes, parents arrive for pickup 3:30 PM - Event ends Workshops Learn AI by Making Games with Phippy! Taught by Cassandra Chin What if you could dream up a game & bring it to life with AI? In this hands-on workshop, kids will team up with an AI coding assistant to create their own playable 2D games using the open source Godot game engine & colorful Phippy & Friends characters. From treasure hunts to tricky mazes, they'll choose the adventure & help shape the rules. As they build, play, & improve their games, kids will practice giving AI clear instructions, checking its work, & solving problems when things don't go as planned. Along the way, they'll discover that AI can help write the code, but they're the game designers in charge! No previous coding or game-making experience is needed, just curiosity & a willingness to experiment, explore, & play! Bio: Cassandra Chin is a keynote speaker, author, podcast host, & computer science student. She has led technology workshops for kids at international conferences since age 13 & is passionate about expanding access to tech education for women, minorities, & underserved communities. What to know before you come: Please bring your own laptop so you can fully participate in the hands-on activities. Space is limited, so if you're unable to attend, please cancel your registration to allow another child to join. We will be taking photos & videos during the event, which will be shared online & featured at the keynote of the AI Engineer World Fair conference that week. Please let us know if you agree to be included in the registration process. Parents or guardians will need to be present to sign their child in at the beginning & sign them out at the end of the event & they welcome to stay & assist your child. No lunch provided, please bring your snack & water Call for Volunteers We're looking for volunteers to support kids during the hands-on workshops. Parents & those with some technical background are invited to help guide & inspire kids as they build & explore. Please register at Open Google Form We can't wait to build with you!

jc_culture_10004836_2026_10_04_rent_the_.summary: Experience the groundbreaking Tony Award-winning musical and Pulitzer Prize-winning drama that defined a generation. Presented at Art House Productions during the 30th anniversary year of its original premiere, RENT follows a vibrant community of artists, musicians, and dreamers in New York City’s East Village as they pursue their passions, navigate love and loss, and strive to make a meaningful impact on the world around them. Set against the backdrop of the AIDS crisis, poverty, addiction, economic uncertainty, and a rapidly changing city, these artists discover the power of friendship, the importance of creative expression, and the enduring strength of community. Featuring iconic songs and an unforgettable rock score, RENT celebrates resilience, human connection, and the transformative role of the arts in times of hardship. This production is especially meaningful as part of Art House Productions’ 25th Anniversary Season. Founded in the wake of September 11, 2001, Art House was created to bring people together through the arts during a time of profound loss and uncertainty. Thirty years after its premiere, RENT remains as relevant, timeless, and inspiring as ever, reminding us all to measure our lives in love.
